digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure — subprocess and network sentinels
propositions: Five real-subprocess reap tests spend ~1.01s each waiting for a 1s timeout deadline to expire due to a blanket module-wide autouse fixture, creating load-dependent flakes.
Three reap tests assert on child-side setup (pidfile, spawn counter, flushed stdout) but ordering depends on the injected window exceeding interpreter startup time, not on explicit synchronization.
A read-retry test inherits a 1s timeout ceiling as an implicit pass condition, creating a latent flake in the opposite direction when the child must complete two sequential spawns.
The snapshot stall-abort test injects a 2s low-speed window even though a 1s window is sufficient and already proven by a sibling test.

Setup races must be closed by explicit readiness gates and observable file markers rather than by tuning timeout numbers, so that smaller windows make hangs more certain without introducing real-time dependence.
